subject: Marketplace bundle SKUs / reseller pass-through & allocation
messages:
From: Mike Reynolds <mike@cloudops.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace bundle SKUs / reseller pass-through & allocation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — quick intro: I’m Mike (procurement) at CloudOps Inc. We’re evaluating a ~$1.2M Azure private offer for our platform bundle and need to confirm a couple of items before we proceed to legal/procurement:

- Can Redwood support bundling multiple SKUs in a single Azure private offer that we present as a single line on our internal PO? We’d like to map three components (runtime tokens, embeddings, and a managed feature flag quota) into a single bundle SKU.
- On reseller pass-through: our channel partner requires a 20% gross margin on the Redwood line item. How does Redwood handle reseller allocation on the invoice and marketplace payout? Do you support pass-through allocations that show the reseller margin on the invoice so our partner can reconcile?
- Is there a list-price floor required by Azure marketplace for private offers that would block us from offering our partner the margin we need?

Attached are our minimum order quantity requirements for the bundle (CloudOps_MOQ_requirements.pdf). If you can send a short mutual action plan and a sample invoice flow that demonstrates reseller pass-through, that’ll help speed approval.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow? My availability 9–11am PT.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Reynolds
Head of Procurement, CloudOps Inc
procurement@cloudops.com
Attachment: CloudOps_MOQ_requirements.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mike Reynolds <mike@cloudops.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace bundle SKUs / reseller pass-through & allocation

Hi Mike — appreciated the note and the MOQs. Looping in Ben (channel) and Laura (pricing) so we can cover both marketplace mechanics and partner allocation.

Short answers up front:
- Yes — Azure private offers can present a single consolidated line item for a bundle, provided we register the bundle as a single SKU in the marketplace listing. We typically create a bundle SKU that maps to multiple internal meters in our billing backend; externally it appears as one line on the PO/invoice.
- Reseller pass-through: we support showing a reseller allocation on the invoice (line-level pass-through percentages) for Azure private offers, and can also surface that in the marketplace payout CSV so your partner can reconcile. There are a few prerequisites (see below).
- List-price floors: Azure enforces a minimum list-price for private offers in certain regions and for certain offer categories. In our experience, price floors are usually not binding for enterprise-level list prices, but we’ll confirm for your SKU once you share target list price.

I’ve attached a pricing ladder that shows example list prices, recommended channel margins, and the invoice representation (redwood-pricing-ladder.xlsx). A couple of actions we need from you so we can finalize:

1) Confirm target list price for the bundle and desired reseller gross margin (you mentioned ~20%).
2) Confirm the partner entity (legal name + marketplace publisher id) so we can set up the pass-through allocation.
3) Do you require the partner to be on the marketplace payout or will you invoice the partner directly? (Different flows; marketplace payout is simpler for reconciliation but requires the partner to be a registered marketplace publisher).

Proposed next steps / MAP:
- Today: confirm (1)–(3) above.
- Tomorrow: 30-min call to align mechanics and timing.
- Within 48 hours: Redwood to send sample private-offer invoice and payout CSV export.
- Within 5 business days: Agreement and PO routing to legal/Docusign.

If that works, Ben — can you confirm whether a 20% target margin is feasible from a channel enablement/commission perspective?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Sales — Cloud & Marketplace
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-pricing-ladder.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Marketplace bundle SKUs / reseller pass-through & allocation

Karthik — thanks, that’s helpful. A couple clarifications after reviewing the ladder:

> On 2026-10-29, karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
> > I’ve attached a pricing ladder that shows example list prices, recommended channel margins, and the invoice representation.

We’d like to target a 20% gross margin for the partner. For internal approval we need:
- A sample invoice that shows the Redwood bundle line and the allocated reseller margin line (so finance can see the pass-through).
- An example payout CSV or statement format that the marketplace would generate so the partner can reconcile receipts.
- Confirmation that activating the private offer won’t require the partner to change their existing billing relationship with us (i.e., partner prefers not to be re-registered as a publisher). If marketplace payout requires that, we might instead route the Redwood line through our invoice and pay the partner separately.

Also — can you confirm any timing constraints if we need the private offer active by Nov 15? We need legal / procurement signoff and a PO in that window.

Can do a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT. Sending a calendar invite.

—Mike

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mike Reynolds <mike@cloudops.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace bundle SKUs / reseller pass-through & allocation

Mike — great, 10am PT works. Quick responses to your asks and a proposed MAP we can turn into milestone deliverables on the call: 

- Sample invoice / payout: see attached pricing ladder for the line-level layout; we’ll finalize a real sample invoice and a sample marketplace payout CSV during the call. We can generate a pseudo-payout using your partner legal name to demonstrate columns used for reconciliation.
- Publisher registration: marketplace payout that flows directly to the partner requires the partner to be registered in the marketplace. If they prefer not to, the alternative is to have CloudOps pay Redwood and then pay the partner separately; Redwood supports both flows but keep in mind it changes who receives the marketplace credits and the settlement path.
- Timing for Nov 15: doable if we lock list price and partner legal entity by Nov 3 and we have a signed PO by Nov 9 — that gives us time to configure the private offer and run validation tests.

Mutual action plan (draft) — will convert to a shared doc on the call:
1) By Nov 3: CloudOps confirms target list price and partner legal name/publisher id.
2) By Nov 5: Redwood sends sample invoice + payout CSV, and a one-page summary of payout flow options.
3) By Nov 9: CloudOps issues PO and routing instructions (marketplace payout vs direct pass-through).
4) Nov 10–14: Testing + private offer activation.
5) Nov 15: Go-live.

I’ll open a DocuSign envelope for the PO once we have the numbers — sending the link post-call.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Sales — Cloud & Marketplace
Redwood Inference
